terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the restock sheet here and read where Node stops.

tasks.title: Count the wax jars
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/restock.js`, Node stops at the line that prints the wax jars left. Fix it so it prints `Wax jars left:` followed by the number in `waxJars`. The line that makes `waxJars` is right as it is.

Check runs the lines of Task 1 alone, with another number in `waxJars`, and looks for that line with that number.
nextSteps: Run `node src/restock.js`. Node stops at Task 3 first; the lesson says why. Fix that one first, or read on and come back.
Once Node gets to Task 1, read the kind of error and the name in its message.
Compare that name, letter by letter, with the line that makes it.
Fix the line that uses it and run the file again.
hints: The error names a name Node does not know. Look for a name that is almost the same in the line above.
Capital letters count: two names that differ only in one capital are two different names to Node.
The name is made as `waxJars`, with a capital J. Use it exactly like that in the `console.log` line.

tasks.title: Take the sold candles off the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, the cedar count starts with the candles delivered and should then lose the ones sold, but Node stops when the count changes. Fix it so it prints `On the shelf:` followed by the candles delivered minus the candles sold.

Check runs the lines of Task 2 alone, with its own numbers in `cedarDelivered` and `cedarSold`, and looks for that line with the right count.
nextSteps: Run the file until Node stops under Task 2, and read the kind of error.
The message says what kind of variable is being changed. Find where that variable is made.
Ask whether this count should be able to change.
Fix it so the count changes, and run the file again.
hints: The line Node stops at is not the mistake. It does what it should. Look at how the variable was made.
A `const` keeps its first value forever. A count that changes during the day needs the other keyword.
Make `cedarOnShelf` with `let` instead of `const`, and keep the line that takes the sold candles off.

tasks.title: Write the label in capitals
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, the label starts as the customer's name and should then become the same name in capital letters, but Node cannot even read the file. Fix it so it prints `Label:` followed by the customer's name in capitals.

Check runs the lines of Task 3 alone, with another name in `customerName`, and looks for that line with the name in capitals.
nextSteps: Run the file: this is the error Node shows first, before any line runs.
Read the name in the message, and find every line where that name is made.
Ask whether the second line means to make a new variable or to change the one that is there.
Fix it and run the file again.
hints: The message says a name has already been declared. Declared means made with `let` or `const`.
A name can be made only once. To change it afterwards you write the name, `=` and the new value, with no keyword in front.
Remove `let` from the second line, so it reads `label = label.toUpperCase()`.

tasks.title: Make the city code
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, the city code should be the first three letters of the city, without the spaces around it, in capital letters. Node stops on that line. Fix it so it prints `City code:` followed by the code.

Check runs the lines of Task 4 alone, with another city, spaces included, in `city`, and looks for that line with the right code.
nextSteps: Run the file until Node stops under Task 4, and read the whole message.
The message names something that is not a function. Look at each dot on the line and what comes before it.
Compare the line with how the lesson uses a method.
Fix it and run the file again.
hints: The message names `city.trim.slice`. Read it as: the thing called `slice` on `city.trim` is not a function.
A method only runs when it has round brackets after its name. Without them, `city.trim` is the method itself, not the trimmed city.
